newsitem.title: GABON: Voting extended in chaotic Gabon poll rerun.
newsitem.headline: Voting extended in chaotic Gabon poll rerun.

text.p: Gabon electoral authority on Sunday ordered polls to stay open indefinitely to allow more people to vote in a confused partial rerun of local elections.

A member of the independent National Electoral Commission said the order was given after organisational problems prevented many people from casting ballots in the rerun of elections in the capital Libreville and the town of Fougamou.
The same logistics problems that dogged the main poll on October 20 leading to violence and the cancellation of the vote in the two cities again marred Sunday's voting.
Electoral lists and ballots were not available at most polling stations in the capital, which accounts for about half the population in the country of about 1.2 million people.
In one polling station, the voter list available was different from that of the National Elections Commission.
"Many names do not appear on the voter lists," a frustrated voter said after polls opened at 8 a.m. (0700 GMT). They were scheduled to close officially at 6 p.m.
Turnout appeared even lower than last month's vote, with many politicians and some of their followers campaigning in the interior for December 1 legislative elections.
There were no reports of violence in Libreville or Fougamou, where a fight prevented voting on October 20. The election commission scrapped results in Libreville, blaming organisational problems.
President Omar Bongo's Gabonese Democratic Party and Father Paul M'Ba Abessole's opposition Woodcutters' Party won most seats decided last month.
The two parties are vying for control of Libreville city hall, with Abessole and Bongo's housing minister Jean-Francois Ntoutoume Emane battling for mayor.
